mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registration Office of the competent District Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Hague Apostille states: original certified extract previously authenticated by the issuing registry followed by an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular legalization. Path B for non-member states: certified extract followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then consular legalization by the destination state's consular post in the Republic of Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and shall never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Clearance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, competent District Tax Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Apostille states: official certificate issued by the National Tax Service followed by an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; no consular step. Path B for non-member states: official certificate followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then legalization by the competent consulate of the destination state. The two authentication routes are parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney approving incorporation, UBO declaration, and banking signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Apostille states: notarized board resolution followed by an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; consular legalization is not required. Path B for non-member states: notarized board resolution followed by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then consular legalization at the destination state's consulate. Do not chain an Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy including corporate object clause for wholesale of non-ferrous copper cathodes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company and Court Registration Office of the competent District Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Apostille states: certified copy issued by the company and confirmed by the court registry, then an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea when used abroad; no consular legalization. Path B for non-member states: certified copy through Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and destination consulate legalization. Select only one route depending on the receiving jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for corporate account and Documentary Letter of Credit facility
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Maintaining Korean commercial bank of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A for Apostille states: original bank reference letter issued on bank letterhead, signed by a branch manager, then an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea when the recipient is a Hague Convention state; no consular step. Path B for non-member states: original bank reference letter with bank seal, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and consular legalization by the destination state's consulate. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be applied sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before formation, counsel shall screen every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, and counterparty against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated sanctions, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, and all applicable Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance designations. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates; the file must include source of wealth, source of funds, corporate structure evidence, independent senior partner approval, and annual re-screening. A positive match or unexplained PEP nexus is an automatic disqualification for incorporation and documentary LC onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea requires the registered corporate name to be written in Hangeul; a foreign-language trade name may be used only as a supplementary name together with the Hangeul registered name. For Yuhan Hoesa, the name must include the limited liability designator 'Yuhan Hoesa' at the end. The four-tier naming convention consists of: (1) the business form designator; (2) the distinctive trade name element; (3) the business purpose clause; and (4) the administrative district of the registered office. Phonetic transliteration from English or other scripts must be consistent with the Korean Commercial Act and must not create confusion with an existing registered trade name in the same administrative district.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Internet Registration Office rejects the proposed name, counsel shall obtain the written rejection notice, extract the exact statutory ground, and file a written objection with the competent District Court Registry within two weeks. Where the rejection is based on a conflicting trade name, counsel may amend the proposed distinctive element and refile before expiration of the reservation window. Where the registry asserts a prohibited token, counsel must request prior ministerial clearance from the competent authority and attach the approval to the refiled application. Thereafter, an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the competent administrative court; the petition must demonstrate non-infringement and non-confusion under Commercial Act Article 254.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable for this industry. The National Tax Service will reject a virtual address for value-added tax registration and corporate tax invoice issuance for a wholesale copper cathode trader, and Korean commercial banks will reject the account and documentary Letter of Credit facility without physical substance. Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a verifiable registered office in the Republic of Korea evidenced by a lease in the entity name, a physical nameplate, dedicated staff, business telephone, meeting room, and access to original books and records. A serviced office may qualify only if it provides a dedicated private workspace, lease agreement, utility invoices, and bank-visible substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) external signage with the registered corporate name; (2) original lease and rent receipts; (3) utility statements; (4) payroll and withholding tax filings; (5) corporate seal and statutory records; (6) third-party warehouse or logistics contracts supporting copper cathode transit storage; (7) LME warrant and documentary LC transaction files; (8) board and shareholder minutes ledger. Quantified risk: high, estimated above 40% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the District Tax Office or Korea Customs Service within the first 12 months of operation for this high-volume physical wholesale trading profile.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last amended), Chapter 12 on Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), Articles 287-2 through 287-74; read together with the corporate registration provisions of the Registration of Non-Contentious Litigation Cases Act and the Supreme Court Registration Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Company; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, with all required statutory exhibits
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Yuhan Hoesa. The incorporators may fix the member capital contributions in the Articles of Incorporation at any amount, but all subscribed cash contributions must be fully deposited into a blocked escrow account at a licensed Korean bank before the registration application is submitted. The bank certificate of capital contribution deposit must be filed with the registry court, and the escrowed funds cannot be released or used for operations until the Certificate of Corporate Registration has been issued by the district court. Non-cash contributions, if any, must be verified by an independent appraiser and described in the Articles of Incorporation. Capitalization should nevertheless be set at a level commercially sufficient for the intended LME warrant transfer and documentary letter of credit trading operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA 

 Resolution No. 2025-001, adopted unanimously by the initial directors in writing on the date set out in the minutes. WHEREAS, the Company has been formed to engage in the wholesale physical arbitrage trade of Grade A refined copper cathodes and related non-ferrous metals under ISIC 4662 and NAICS 423510; and WHEREAS, the initial directors have been designated in the Articles of Incorporation to exercise the powers and duties imposed by the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS: 

 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The aggregate member capital contributions subscribed in the Articles of Incorporation are hereby acknowledged and accepted in full. The Representative Director is directed to enforce payment of all subscribed contributions, deposit each cash contribution into a blocked escrow corporate account maintained at a licensed Korean bank, and obtain from the bank a capital contribution deposit certificate. No contribution funds shall be released to the Company until the corporate registration has been completed and the certificate of incorporation issued. 

 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [full street address, Republic of Korea], and that address is declared to be the statutory register office, place of keeping the register of members and accounting records, and address for service of legal process. 

 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company is authorized to open demand, settlement, and foreign exchange accounts at [bank name, branch], and the Representative Director together with one other designated director are appointed as co-signatories. All LME warrant transfer proceeds and documentary letter of credit payments shall be received through an account in the Company name and managed under the Company AML and sanctions compliance policy. 

 4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS. [name of individual] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [name of individual] is appointed Director and Chief Financial Officer; and [name of individual] is appointed Auditor and Compliance Officer. Each appointed officer accepts the office, and the Representative Director is authorized to execute all corporate registration filings and tax, customs, and banking documents required to commence operations. 

 5. POST-INCORPORATION ACTS. The corporate legal counsel and officers are authorized to complete the corporate registration with the District Court Registration Office, to file the business registration with the National Tax Service, to report the trade business to the Korea Customs Service, and to take all lawful steps necessary to make the Company operational. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Pre-Incorporation Documentary Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice, typically located in the district of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation for Yuhan Hoesa, including the corporate name, registered office address, precise business purpose covering wholesale trade of non-ferrous metal ores and refined copper cathodes, the amount of member capital contributions, contribution payment method, number of directors, term of office, and indemnity provisions. All incorporators must appear before, or be represented by a duly appointed attorney-in-fact before, a Korean notary public to execute the Articles by signature or adjudicated seal. Non-resident incorporators must present apostilled or legalized passports and identity documents, together with a certified power of attorney if acting through a domestic representative. The notary will certify the date and authenticity of execution, which certificate is a mandatory precondition to the court registration of a Korean limited liability company.
required_dossiers: Korean-language draft Articles of Incorporation
Apostilled or legalized passports of all incorporators
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if a domestic agent acts for a foreign incorporator
Korean seal registration certificate (injejang) or overseas equivalent
Written consent of each initial director and auditor
Capital contribution schedule and bank source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because of incomplete identity documentation or a defective translation, cure by obtaining a certified Korean translation, completing the missing apostilles, and resubmitting to the same or another notary within two business days. If the notarial objection is based on an unlawful or ambiguous business purpose, amend the Articles of Incorporation to narrow the purpose to wholesale metal trading and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Contribution Escrow Account and Verification of Fully Paid Member Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, for example Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, or Hana Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the court registration application is filed, open a temporary blocked escrow account in the name of the intended Yuhan Hoesa, or held jointly by the incorporators through the Korean notary or attorney-in-fact, solely for receiving the initial member capital contributions. Transfer the subscribed cash contributions in Korean won or convert lawful foreign currency through the bank, and obtain a bank certificate of capital contribution deposit stating the account holder, the amount deposited, the account number, and the escrow condition. The bank will require beneficial ownership disclosure, source of funds evidence, and sanctions screening. The account must remain blocked until the corporate registration certificate is issued, after which funds are released to the corporate operating account. Non-cash contributions must be appraised and described in a separate valuation report satisfying the Commercial Act requirements.
required_dossiers: Passport and apostilled identity documents for all contributing members
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney for bank account opening and transaction instruction
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds forms required by the Korean bank
Capital contribution remittance instruction and foreign exchange declaration if funds originate outside Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced KYC, OECD Common Reporting Standard, or sanctions-related queries, provide corrected beneficial ownership charts, structural diagrams, and underlying trade documentation for the copper cathode business. If a particular bank rejects the escrow arrangement, approach another licensed bank and restart the process; no court filing should be made until a valid capital contribution deposit certificate has been obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation together with all statutory exhibits. The registry court will examine whether the Articles of Incorporation have been notarized, whether the capital contribution deposit certificate is valid, whether the directors and auditor have accepted office, and whether the registered office address is lawfully located within the court jurisdiction. Pay the registration and license tax, the local education tax, and the court filing fee through the court e-payment system. Upon approval, the court enters Yuhan Hoesa into the corporate registration register and issues a certified Certificate of Corporate Registration. The legal existence of the company commences on the date of this court registration, not on the date of the notarization or the capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of Incorporation in the court-prescribed form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of capital contribution deposit
Consent and appointment certificates for the Representative Director, directors, and Auditor
Seal registration certificate of the Representative Director or proof of registered seal impression
Receipt of payment of registration tax, local education tax, and court filing fee
Lease contract or right-to-use document for the registered office, or landlord consent
Power of attorney if a Korean attorney submits the application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or suspension notice because of a missing exhibit, an ambiguous business purpose, or an unlawful office address, cure by filing the corrected document or amendment within the court-specified grace period, usually ten to fourteen days. If the proposed corporate name is rejected, select a new distinguishable Korean corporate name and refile without payment of an additional registration tax. If the court dismisses the application, the attorney may file a reappeal or prepare a fresh application package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Corporate Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Head of the competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service through the HomeTax one-portal system (www.hometax.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty calendar days after the court registration, submit an Application for Business Registration Certificate to obtain the corporate registration number used for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and employment withholding tax. The tax office will review the court-issued Certificate of Corporate Registration, the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the lease or right-to-use document for the registered office, and the identity documents of the Representative Director. After approval, the National Tax Service will assign the Yuhan Hoesa a business registration number and a VAT registration number. This step is mandatory before opening an unrestricted corporate bank account, issuing invoices, executing documentary letters of credit, or filing customs declarations. If the company has no resident director, a tax representative must be appointed and the representative director passport must be translated and apostilled.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration issued by the district court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease contract or landlord consent for the registered office address
Passport and resident registration card of the Representative Director or foreign equivalent
Corporate seal certificate
Bank certificate of the corporate capital account
Power of attorney or tax representative appointment letter
Business registration application form completed in Korean
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional evidence of a fixed place of business, provide the utility bill, floor plan, management fee receipt, and landlord identity confirmation. If the application is suspended due to an address mismatch or an unpaid national tax issue attributable to a predecessor, file an explanatory memorandum, correct the address, and settle any outstanding liabilities before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Korean Customs Trade Business Report and Metal Commodity Supply Chain KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single-window system and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for trade and strategic goods screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the Yuhan Hoesa will conduct wholesale physical arbitrage of Grade A refined copper cathodes and may settle trades through LME warrant transfers and documentary letters of credit, file a trade business report under the Foreign Trade Act to obtain import and export code authorization. The report is submitted electronically through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal using the business registration number and corporate seal. Complete the associated KTNET registration for international trade and submit beneficial ownership and sanctions screening documentation. Copper cathode purchases and sales must be KYC-checked against the counterparty, the LME warrant issuer, the warehouse, and the shipping or freight forwarder. If the company operates its own physical warehouse within Korea, an additional warehouse business report must be filed with the municipal Si/Gun/Gu office, and fire safety and structural clearances will apply.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate from the National Tax Service
Certificate of Corporate Registration from the district court Registry Office
Detailed business scope including ISIC 4662 and HS headings for refined copper cathodes
Beneficial ownership declaration
KYC and AML forms for each counterparty and bank, including LME warrant and documentary LC evidence
Lease agreement or warehouse service agreement if physical storage is involved
Importer-exporter authorization form for UNI-PASS and KTNET
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Korea Customs Service rejects the trade business report for incomplete foreigner documentation, resubmit with apostilled passports, certified corporate registration documents, and sanctioned-party screening results. If the HS classification of copper cathodes is queried, provide the refinery certificate, assay analysis, and LME warrant specification sheet along with a revised customs declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service and Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy for cross-border trade reporting; for any ancillary warehouse operation, the municipal Si/Gun/Gu office under the Warehousing Industry Act
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for wholesale non-ferrous metal trading under ISIC 4662; the applicable administrative filings are the trade business report under the Foreign Trade Act for import and export activity and, if the company operates its own storage facilities, the warehouse business report under the Warehousing Industry Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the wholesale trading of copper cathodes does not involve a physical installation requiring environmental authorization; if an ancillary covered warehouse or industrial facility is created, the competent agency would be the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea through the Korea Environment Corporation and the municipal environmental licensing office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - full Environmental Impact Assessment and prior environmental review are not required for pure wholesale trade of non-ferrous metals and copper cathodes under ISIC 4662; a Full EIA Report would apply only if a future project falls within the project categories listed in the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, such as a large non-ferrous smelter or a large logistics and storage facility
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge thresholds apply to office-based wholesale trading. If a future covered facility is established, the applicable quantitative standards will be determined by the facility capacity and waste stream under the Clean Air Conservation Act, the Clean Water Conservation Act, and the Chemicals Control Act, including pollutant concentration limits and hazardous substance handling permit requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For office and trading operations, Yuhan Hoesa must be covered by the landlord statutory fire safety completion certificate and must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a basic workplace safety plan and emergency evacuation plan. If the company operates a copper cathode warehouse in Korea, the facility must obtain a fire-fighting system completion inspection and fire safety certificate from the National Fire Agency, complete a structural load and rack stability inspection by a qualified engineer, and satisfy all storage and escape route requirements before commencement of operations; for workplaces with employees, annual workplace safety and health inspections through the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency may apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Customs export declarations are cleared through Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities: (1) appoint a tax representative in Korea if the foreign entity has no domestic place of business; (2) file an Application for Business Registration (Business Registration Certificate) with the Local District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the tax representative or the Korean place of business; (3) attach the foreign entity's incorporation certificate, board resolution appointing the tax representative, a notarized power of attorney, the tax representative's Korean resident registration or business registration, and a Korean business lease if applicable; (4) after verification, NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which also serves as the Korean VAT ID. Domestic Yuhan Hoesa: the representative director files the same Application for Business Registration with the competent Local District Tax Office within 20 days of business commencement, attaching articles of incorporation, shareholder register, lease agreement for the registered office, and director identification; NTS issues the Business Registration Number that acts as the corporate TIN and VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not recognise a check-the-box pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; the entity is mandatorily taxed as a separate domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available. Group consolidation filing is not applicable to this base metal wholesale entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold for general taxpayers; a Yuhan Hoesa, being a corporation, must register for VAT before commencing business. The simplified-taxpayer threshold of KRW 48,000,000 in annual taxable supplies applies only to natural persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued as electronic tax invoices under Article 32 of the VAT Act and transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system no later than the day following issuance. Each e-invoice carries an NTS-assigned electronic tax invoice number, a digital certificate, and an anti-fraud electronic token. Korea does not impose a continuous real-time fiscal clearance API for B2B wholesale transactions; however, export declarations are validated through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS, and VAT e-invoices are submitted using HomeTax DTD with API/EDI integration. Non-compliance triggers the statutory additional taxes (e.g., 2% of the supply value for failure to issue, 2% for incorrect issuance, plus applicable penalty interest).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 24(1)(1) of the VAT Act, exports of South Korean goods are zero-rated when the goods are deposited in a bonded area, loaded, and transported abroad under an accepted export declaration. For the Grade A refined copper cathode wholesale activity, zero-rating requires an LME warrant transfer or delivery order accompanied by physical export through a Korean customs port; the warrant transfer alone does not justify 0% VAT. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated only if supplied to a non-resident customer and consumed outside Korea, with supporting evidence retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export declaration submitted to Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS and accepted with a unique export serial number)
Bill of Lading (or multimodal transport document) evidencing loading at a Korean port and discharge at a foreign destination
Commercial Invoice and Packing List corresponding exactly to the copper cathode grade, warehouse location, and LME warrant details
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (Inward Remittance Certificate, FIRC) issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank upon collection of export proceeds
LME warrant transfer or delivery order records evidencing title transfer to the non-resident buyer (supporting evidence; does not replace physical export proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audit teams cross-match the Export Declaration status, shipping manifests, and inflows of export proceeds through the foreign exchange information system. If the export zero-rating is not substantiated by the customs and FX settlement documents within the 180-day repatriation deadline, or if the documents are false or backdated, the NTS reverses the zero rating, assesses 10% VAT, adds statutory additional tax under Article 48 of the VAT Act for fraudulent or negligent refunds, imposes a false-invoice additional tax up to 2% of the supply value, and may pursue criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to 50 times the evaded tax. The VAT refunded is clawed back with interest; records must be retained for at least five years after export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised convertibility system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The won is fully convertible for current-account needs, including international trade and business services, and such settlements require only post-event reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity/debt investment and cross-currency funding, are subject to notification, registration, and use of authorised foreign exchange business banks; they are not subject to prior approval in the ordinary course. There is no centralised surrender requirement for export proceeds, which may be retained in foreign-currency accounts at domestic banks. However, profit remittance and repatriation of capital require evidence of the original foreign-investment registration, tax clearance certificates, and audited financial statements, and should be routed through the same banking corridor used for capital injection. The Bank of Korea and MOEF retain macro-prudential levers, including monitoring of speculative inflows and temporary recovery measures. For a copper cathode wholesaler, credibility is enhanced by demonstrating LME-backed invoicing, real trade flows, and corporate tax compliance, allowing unrestricted current-account clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters must recover export proceeds within one year from the export declaration date; extensions are possible with Korea Customs Service or BOK approval for justified causes such as deferred payment terms. Mandatory surrender ratio is 0%: South Korea does not require conversion of export receipts into KRW. Proceeds may be held in foreign-currency accounts or foreign exchange bank accounts and used for trade settlement, FX hedging, and approved capital transactions, subject to Foreign Exchange Information System reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Documentary LC Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low / not legally viable as a primary banking rail. South Korea reserves deposit-taking, foreign exchange, and cross-border settlement services to domestic banks and licensed foreign exchange business entities under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, or Airwallex are not authorised to maintain KRW corporate accounts or clear trade payments for a Korean-domiciled entity absent a partnership with a licensed domestic bank. They may be used only as ancillary payment gateways for low-value expenses, and even then funds must pass through a compliant domestic bank account. Therefore, all treasury operations for KR_YUHANGHOESA should be anchored in Tier-1 Korean commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch KYC interview is the default statutory expectation for opening a Korean corporate account. Under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and BOK AML guidelines, at least one statutory director or a senior authorised officer with full board authority must appear at the bank branch with original passport, corporate seal, and notarised constitutional documents; remote or consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for the initial account. Additional signatories may be appointed via apostilled power of attorney after the account is live. Some banks offer video-assisted interviews for foreign directors, but biometric verification and original document examination are still performed at the branch at final approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial owner behind a newly formed Korean LLC with foreign shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation, memorandum of association, shareholders' register, UBO declaration naming every natural person with more than 25% interest, passport copies with proof of residential address, bank references from home-country banks, and a detailed group structure/organisation chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering risk from copper cathode mis-invoicing or phantom cargo.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial sales contracts containing exact grade of Grade A copper cathode, LME settlement clause, independent third-party inspection certificates from SGS/Cotecna/Alex Stewart, bill of lading, customs declarations, cargo insurance documents, warehouse receipts or LME warrant transfer records, and a written pricing explanation against the LME copper price.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or iterative country-of-origin risk on raw copper materials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificates and smelter/production origin declarations, full supply-chain provenance records, sanctions screening results against OFAC, UN/EU, and South Korean FSS lists, end-use and end-user undertakings from all counterparties, and an internal sanctions compliance policy covering vessel flag checks and transhipment risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual source of wealth or high-frequency turnover for a newly formed trading entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of beneficial owners, three months of current-account bank statements, home-country tax filings and Korean tax filings, evidence of committed capital from directors' declared income or shareholder loan agreements, and a realistic treasury forecast explaining trading volumes, margin requirements, counterparties, and liquidity sources.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor registers the investment with KOTRA or a designated Korean bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remitting funds, obtains a foreign-investment registration certificate, then wires capital via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account to the entity's foreign-currency capital escrow account at a domestic Korean bank. The credited amount must match the registered FDI amount and purpose; the bank issues a foreign capital deposit certificate and performs capital verification. After legal registration of the share increase, funds may be converted into KRW through the designated domestic bank and transferred to the operational current account. All wires must use the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code for foreign direct investment capital settlement; no repatriation is permissible before full registration and tax clearance isshown.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For copper cathode imports and exports, use SWIFT MT103 for operating costs, trade margin calls, freight, insurance, and intercompany financing; use irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) with full set of bills of lading, inspection certificates, LME warrant transfer instructions, and commercial invoices for Grade A copper cathodes; and use Documentary Collections (URC522) for lower-risk counterparties with approved trade credit limits. All payments must reference underlying contracts, carry the correct foreign exchange purpose code, and match the bank's trade finance records to support AML, FX, and customs reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright FX forward contracts with proven real trade exposure and underlying copper cathode contracts
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to manage USD/KRW funding and trade finance interest rate risk
FX options with premium payment and documented hedging rationale
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through international banking books of licensed Korean banks, subject to Bank of Korea reporting and macro-prudential limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local corporate income tax surtax return, including audited financial statements when compulsory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system, and local tax office competent for the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 immediately following the fiscal year end for a December 31 fiscal year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge up to 20 percent of the unpaid tax; unpaid tax collection surcharge of 3 percent within the first 30 days and 5 percent after 30 days, plus daily interest at the statutory underpayment rate; repeated failure may lead to criminal tax prosecution and seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual regular meeting of members approving the annual financial statements, allocation of retained earnings, and reappointment or discharge of executive officers and auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book maintained at the registered office; not filed separately with a governmental registry unless the company is subject to external audit and the minutes are required by a regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year, being no later than March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability for directors and members for corporate acts made without proper approval; failure to establish or maintain the minutes may expose the company to court-ordered dissolution at the request of members or creditors under the Commercial Act; regulatory penalties apply if an external audit report was required and the audit committee or members approval is missing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public accountant audit report on the annual financial statements, filed and publicly disclosed where the company meets statutory size thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (DART system) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants; the report is also attached to the corporate income tax return filed with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three weeks after the regular members meeting that approved the financial statements, effectively by April 21 for a December 31 fiscal year end if the meeting was held by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies up to KRW 30 million for failure to appoint an auditor or submit an audit report; false or misleading audit statements may trigger criminal liability; supervisory sanctions include designation of a different auditor and prohibition of securities issuance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Business Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy / Invest Korea operated through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 each year covering the preceding calendar year of foreign-invested business operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5 million under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for late, false, or omitted reporting; loss of foreign investment incentives including tax reduction or exemption benefits and reinstatement of previously exempted taxes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax returns and related supporting schedules for zero-rated or taxable supplies of copper cathodes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half return by July 25 of the same year; second half return by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing or under-declaration surcharge up to 3 percent of the unpaid tax, additional 0.75 percent per month for overdue amounts, and criminal prosecution for knowingly false invoices; persistent delinquency may trigger the NTS collection procedure and business registration tax lien

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, which equates a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company with a company subject to external audit, an independent certified public accountant audit is compulsory if as of the preceding fiscal year end any one of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (a) total assets on the balance sheet equal or exceed KRW 10 billion; (b) annual turnover from the income statement equal or exceeds KRW 10 billion; or (c) the average number of full-time employees during the fiscal year equals or exceeds 100. The Financial Services Commission may also designate a company as subject to external audit for creditor or shareholder protection, and the National Tax Service may require a certified audit in connection with tax incentive compliance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies listed or otherwise subject to external audit, or with Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for Small and Medium Enterprises (K-GAAP-SME) where the company is an unlisted small or medium sized entity eligible for the simplified framework; all companies must maintain double-entry bookkeeping and comply with the Commercial Act accounting provisions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not operate a separate annual UBO confirmation filing to the commercial registry. Instead, financial institutions are required to perform customer due diligence and identify beneficial owners under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. For a Yuhan Hoesa, changes in membership must be recorded in the register of members and notified to the competent registration office where required. A foreign investor or foreign-invested entity must report share acquisitions, transfers, and material ownership changes to the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days of the triggering event. Failure to maintain accurate registers may invalidate member decisions, restrict dividend distributions, and subject foreign investors to administrative fines.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 per annum including registered office address, corporate secretarial support, and maintaining the statutory registers
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per audit engagement for a copper cathode wholesale trading entity subject to a mandatory external audit under Korean law

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (applicable to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive lower rates of 9%/19%/21% apply below that threshold)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested company tax holidays under Foreign Investment Promotion Act, free-zone incentives (e.g., Free Economic Zones, Jeju International Free City), R&D tax credits up to 25-30% of qualifying R&D expenditures, and capital investment tax credits; no patent box regime currently enacted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서) filed electronically via National Tax Service HomeTax system (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis), with quarterly semi-annual interim prepayment due at the end of sixth month of each fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., March 31 of the following year for a December 31 year-end); extended deadlines available upon application where tax accounts are being audited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate worldwide gross revenue for the fiscal year, including sales of copper cathodes, service fees, and other income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned Korean LLC must report all income derived from both domestic and foreign sources as per Korean domestic law; no limited foreign income exemption except under specific tax treaty provisions. Consider the deemed domestic source income rules if trading through Korean broker or exchanging LME warrants on Korean exchange.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Cost of Goods Sold and Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, related-party costs, depreciation, interest, royalties, and other deductible expenses incurred in producing the revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to affiliates must be arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation. Deductions for management fees require substantive services; excessive fees may be reclassified as dividends. Withholding taxes on imported services must be considered if the service is deemed sourced in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable income after applying non-deductible expenses, statutory reserves, and net operating loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure losses from branches or permanent establishments of foreign entities are not mixed; Korean LLC is a separate tax resident, so its losses are fully available against future Korean profits within the 10-year carryforward window, subject to the continuity-of-business requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Income Tax Computed at Statutory Rates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate tax rates: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, 24% on the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No preferential rate for non-resident shareholders; the LLC is taxed as a Korean domestic entity. Tax assessments may include additional 10% surtax on under-reported income and 20% on fraudulent underreporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Foreign Income Tax Credit and Incentive Adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income, R&D credits, temporary investment credits, and other incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-owned pass-through treated as controlled foreign corporation? Here LLC is not pass-through; no look-through. Ensure evidence of foreign tax credits with translated tax payment certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Final Tax Payable / Refund and Withholding Reconciliation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total corporate tax due after credits and prepayments, including individual withholding and VAT-adjusted items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border dividend distributions to the Korean LLC are subject to dividend withholding of 20% (plus 2% local surtax) unless reduced by treaty. Even though the LLC is the taxpayer, final settlement must reconcile distribution withholding and entertainment expense limits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of all international related-party transactions with amounts, counterparty jurisdiction, and transfer-pricing method selected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be submitted if aggregate related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion. Include full local file contents for copper cathode purchases/sales with related ROW entities; failure to provide may result in lump-sum estimation by tax authority.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of the unpaid tax for under-reported income, 40% for fraudulent non-reporting; daily surcharges of 0.022% (max 9% over 48 months) for unpaid tax; criminal penalties under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act up to 3 years imprisonment or fine not exceeding 3 times the evaded tax for simple evasion, and up to 5 years or fine of up to 5 times for aggravated evasion by a company officer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividend withholding tax (plus 2% local income tax surcharge, aggregate 22%) on dividends paid by the Korean LLC to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under an applicable income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the residence jurisdiction, issued within the most recent year, including the beneficial owner statement; (2) submit a treaty relief application using Form 'Application for Non-resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction' to the NTS branch where the payer files, before or at the time of the distribution; (3) substantiate beneficial ownership by providing an ownership chart, minutes of the dividend resolution, and evidence of economic substance (no conduit or pass-through arrangement); (4) if treaty allows a lower rate, the payer may apply based on the submitted documents; otherwise the payer must withhold at domestic rate and the recipient may file a refund claim within 3 years from the end of the taxable year. For copper cathode trading, ensure no permanent establishment in Korea triggers full Korean taxation on business profits rather than final withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalty paid to non-residents: domestic statutory WHT 20% plus 2% local surtax (total 22%). Under most DTA, Korean source interest is exempt or reduced to 10-15% (e.g., OECD/US treaty 10%); royalties are generally reduced to 10-15% (e.g., 10% for patents under most treaties). Must file the same TRC/beneficial-ownership protocol with the withholding agent to apply the reduced rate at source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and submitted when cross-border related-party transaction values exceed KRW 5 billion (approx. USD 3.8 million) in a business year; Master File is required if the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion; CbCR applies for groups with revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although South Korea does not have a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) law similar to UAE, the Korean Tax Authorities apply the core income-generating activities (CIGA) concept via Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) rules, substance-over-form doctrine under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, and the domestic-source income deeming provisions. The Korean LLC must demonstrate that it performs the actual commercial risk-taking and decision-making for copper trading (e.g., negotiating terms, taking delivery risks, holding LME warrants ownership) and has sufficient personnel, offices, and bank accounts. Otherwise, profits can be reallocated to the non-resident parent or treated as constructive dividends subject to WHT.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating revenue from copper cathode sales by invoicing at artificially low prices to an offshore affiliate in a low-tax jurisdiction, shifting profit outside Korea and claiming fake export exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (2019 rev.); penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax (administrative negligence surcharge of 40% of the underreported tax). Aggregate withholding non-compliance adds 15% surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Article 42 of the Framework Act on National Taxes: the director who actually controlled the evasion is jointly liable for the corporate tax plus penalties. Criminal liability: up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine equal to 5 times the evaded tax; when the violation is committed by the corporation, the director can be personally blacklisted by the NTS and prohibited from leaving the country (travel ban/출국금지) pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC exists on paper only, lacking a physical office, employees, and actual board decision-making; it routes title transfers of copper cathodes between foreign affiliates and repatriates profits as 'dispatcher fees' without any substantive activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may disregard the entity as a sham under Article 14, apply the substance-over-form principle, and impute all income to the ultimate non-resident parent, leading to a 40% negligence penalty on underreported income and denial of VAT input credits. Additionally, the company's registration can be cancelled under the Commercial Act for sham management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties via joint liability under Article 42; criminal prosecution for breach of duty under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (similar to fraud). The court may issue a compensation order against the director for the full underpaid corporate tax. Travel restrictions and immigration blacklisting are routinely applied to directors of offshore shell structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using falsified LME warrant transfers and documentary letters of credit to over-invoice copper cathode imports/exports, facturing trade flows to disguise proceeds from illegal activity; failure to report suspicious transactions under the Financial Transactions Reports Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 6 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, failure to file a suspicious transaction report (STR) is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years or a criminal fine of up to KRW 20 million (approx. USD 15,000). The Korea Customs Service may also impose administrative penalties up to KRW 100 million for false trade declarations under the Customs Act, and seize commodities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who intentionally conceal trade-based money laundering are criminally liable; imprisonment up to 10 years under the Proceeds of Crime Act for the predicate offense money-laundering. The court may order asset confiscation or retrieve equivalent value from the director's personal estate. Directors face blacklisting from the financial system and are barred from openings bank accounts; daily fines of KRW 10,000 per day for noncompliance of reporting obligations may be imposed.
